To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mobile CMY-β-lactamases, which have emerged in clinical isolates, were mobilized independently and directly from three Aeromonospecies, which were isolated from fish.
three different CMY-1-like β-lactamase genes were mobilized independently, and hence, that these genes have a common origin in three different Aeromonas species.
three CMY/MOX variants were mobilized independently, and that their mobile loci were highly similar to chromosomal ampC loci of three Aeromonas spp.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin of CMX-family β-lactmases and provides a new insight into the emergence and evolution of mobile antibiotic resistance determinants in the environment.
the mobilization of the chromosomal ampCs of A. sanarellyi, A. caviiae and A. media and the emergence of the CMY-1, MOx-1 and MOX-2 β-lactamase variants.
the evolution and emergence and spread of antibiotic resistance genes in bacterial pathogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MOX-2, MOX-1 and MOX-3 were mobilized independently, and that MOX-3 and MOX-4 were mobilized from the same chromosomal ampC gene.
the CMY-1 family of β-lactamase genes was derived from a single ancestral ampC gene, which was present in Aeromonas sanarelleii.

the CMY-1 family of AmpC β-lacatamases is a group of enzymes which are found in both mobile and non-mobile forms, with some mobile forms having been mobilized from the chromosomal amp C genes of different Aeromonas species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
three CMY-type β-lactamase genes (CMY-1, MOY-2, MOX-9) were mobilized from Aeromonas sanarella (MOX-1), A. cavia (MOX-2) and A. media (MOX-9).
the chromosomal ampCs of Aeromonas sanarrellii, Aeromonads cavie, and Aeromonas cavaie are ancestral to CMY-1, CMY-2 and CMY-9 respectively.
CMY-1, MOXA-1, MOXB-1 and MOXC-1 originated from the ampC genes of Aeromonas sanarellicomplex, Aeromonas cavaiecomplex and Aeromonas mediacomplex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mobilization of CMY-β-lactamases from the chromosome of Aeromonas species may be more frequent than previously assumed.
the CMY-1, MOY-1, and MOX-2 genes were mobilized independently, and that MOX-9 was mobilized independently from the MOX-1 gene.
mobile antibiotic resistance genes are not only transferred between different bacterial species but can also be mobilized from within the same genus.
